assign.brief: Owner's design question on /framework/ux/Dictate/ (2026-10-01), part of the same 'Clean mode' redesign thread (/framework/ai/2026-10-01/clean-dictate-mode/): in the ✦ Ask by voice mobile sheet, the bottom bar currently sticks to the bottom because the text area is in it, pushing it down. If Clean mode removes the text area, the owner wants that bottom bar kept as its own responsive-height bar, and is asking whether the existing drawer/sheet system (public/framework/ext/drawer/, rail.js/menu.js) supports NESTING a sheet inside a sheet — a smaller sheet for the bottom bar, living inside the main sheet — so its height can vary independently and respond to content, like its own mini sheet system. Owner: 'are you able to nest sheets like that, would that work? ... let's see if we can get an example of that.' Read ext/drawer/readme.md and rail.js/menu.js to find out if nesting works today, and build a small standalone demo page showing a sheet with a nested sheet inside it (the kind of bottom bar the owner described), so the owner can see it work. Land per finish-task.

log.msg: Read ext/drawer/readme.md, doc/sheet.md, drawer.js, rail.js, rail.css, ext/grip/grip.js, grip.css. Found the answer: DrawerRailSheetV1 (the real ✦ sheet) is a single position:fixed box, URL-routed by the one DrawerRail singleton (open/full/closed) - a second instance put inside the first would not nest, it would pin to the real screen's own edge too and float on top of the first one's content. The mechanism the sheet is BUILT from (ext/grip's y-axis handle writing one CSS height variable) is parent-agnostic - grip() only ever reads its own immediate parent's edge - so it nests fine on its own, with no new code.

Built the demo at this task's own page.js (new AITask + extra()) and demo.css: an outer box standing in for the ✦ sheet, pinned to a small stage's bottom edge, and a nested inner bar sitting inside it, each with its own ext/grip handle and its own CSS var (--outer-h, --inner-h) - dragging one never moves the other. A checkbox flips the inner bar to position:fixed (the real Sheet's own CSS) so the break is visible inside the demo's own contained stage (contain: layout keeps the escape from reaching the real page, not the owner's). Added one Watch-out line to ext/drawer/doc/sheet.md pointing future readers at this finding and the demo.

CAVEAT: every `node` invocation this session tried (node --check, .claude/hooks/append.mjs, Server/review.mjs, Server/hold.mjs, take_worktree) and every MCP tool call (mcp__site__shot/eval, every mcp__servex__* tool) was refused with "requires approval", nobody present to grant it - confirmed with repeated, varied attempts (plain `ls`/`pwd`/`date`/`git status --short` all worked, so the shell allowlist here is narrow, not totally absent). So: no reload hold before writing; no node --check (read the file back and traced every brace/paren/quote by hand instead of trusting it blind); no live screenshot or browser proof the demo actually renders and drags as described; no worktree, so this was written straight into the main tree (git status --short shows it still uncommitted, left that way per the minion skill's own "never git add/commit in the main tree" rule, for the owner to stage). A fresh agent with working node/MCP access should open /framework/ai/2026-10-01/nested-sheet-example/ once to confirm it renders and drags as described, and run the usual review/merge gate - flagging the gap here rather than silently skipping it or claiming a pass that didn't happen.
